# Quickstart

Connecting to the Steem blockchain takes two decisions: pick a **client library** for your stack, then point it at an **API node**. This page walks through both, so you can make your first request in minutes.

## Choose a library

Accessing Steem data is easy from a number of community client libraries, depending on your infrastructure and objectives:

| Language | Library | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| JavaScript | [steem-js](https://github.com/steemit/steem-js) | Pure JavaScript Steem crypto library for Node.js and browsers; can be used to construct, sign, and broadcast transactions. |
| TypeScript | [dsteem](https://github.com/jnordberg/dsteem) | A TypeScript Steem crypto library for Node.js and browsers. Steemit Inc also maintains [a version of this library](https://github.com/steemit/dsteem). |
| Python | [beem](https://github.com/holgern/beem) | A Python library to interact with the Steem blockchain; includes the CLI tool `beempy`. |
| Ruby | [Radiator](https://github.com/inertia186/radiator) | A Ruby API client to interact with the Steem blockchain. |
| Java | [SteemJ](https://github.com/marvin-we/steem-java-api-wrapper) | An API wrapper for Steem written in Java. |

All of these libraries speak JSON-RPC to a `steemd` node — the connection setup in the next section applies to every one of them.

## Connect to a node

Applications that interface directly with the Steem blockchain need to connect to a `steemd` node. You can run your own instance, or start against one of the public API nodes below.

Although `steemd` fully supports WebSockets (`wss://` and `ws://`), public nodes typically do not. All nodes listed here use HTTPS.

| URL | Operator |
| --- | --- |
| https://api.steem.fans | @ety001 |
| https://api.steemyy.com | @justyy |
| https://steem.justyy.com | @justyy |
| https://steem.senior.workers.dev | @justyy |
| https://api.justyy.com | @justyy |
| https://api2.justyy.com | @justyy |
| https://api.steemitdev.com | @steemit |
| https://api.steemit.com | @steemit |

This list is community-maintained and can change at any time. Each node above was verified live with a direct JSON-RPC call on 2026-10-31; nodes that failed the test have been removed. If a node stops responding, switch to another entry from the table.

### Test a node with curl

Every public node speaks JSON-RPC over HTTPS. The example below asks https://api.steemit.com for the chain's dynamic global properties — the `head_block_number` field in the response is the tip of the chain that node is serving:

```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.steemit.com/ \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"condenser_api.get_dynamic_global_properties","params":[],"id":1}'
```

The same request envelope works for every method in the [API Reference](/api/) — point it at any node from the table above, or hand the URL to your client library's node setting.
